messages:
maya: ran a targeted canary for model v3.2-quant4 on the long-doc/legal slices overnight. quick summary below.

olin: pls summary TL;DR

maya: TL;DR: latency p95 +7ms, throughput ~1.03x, semantic-f1 +0.6%, but hallucination (exact-match probes) 0.95% vs prod 0.45% -> exceeds hallucination gate. ran 12h mirrored shadow + 5k sampled sessions.

rachel: are hallucinations correlated to a particular prompt pattern? any examples?

maya: yes, concentrated on instruction-heavy prompts that request "cite" or "regulatory flags". sample failure: 
```
prompt: "Summarize and flag potential compliance issues, list refs."
prod: supplies bullets, no refs
v3.2-q: adds fabricated ref line "Ref: Sec. 12"
```

dominic: our canary config has hallucination_threshold 0.8% (IIRC). did the run auto-fail?

maya: my local gating file: 
- latency_p95_threshold_ms: 180
- perf_delta_pct_allowed: +10
- hallucination_threshold_pct: 0.8
- mrr_delta_pct: -1
This hit the hallucination gate so it should be a hard fail. I paused before triggering rollback to triage.

olin: did you try a different quant profile (nf4-alt) or any quick calibration?

maya: not yet. next steps I propose: 1) force fallback route -> prod for the long-doc route 2) export top-50 hallucination examples to eval bucket 3) run ablation: nf4-alt, raise safety-filter sensitivity, small instruction-tune pass.

dominic: agree. policy: hallucination hard-fail blocks promotion. go ahead and flip the route. @oncall-bot can you run a force-fallback for route=/v3/chat slice=long-doc?

oncall-bot: ACTION: scheduling fallback route=/v3/chat slice=long-doc target=prod reason=\"hallucination_gate:0.95>0.8\" ETA~45s :rotating_light:

rachel: also create an alert: hallucination_rate >0.7% -> page to eng-ml primary. export sample to s3://redwood-internal/evals/1725012345-quant-bridge/ and attach to canary ticket.

maya: done. flipping route now and uploading logs. will run nf4-alt contrastive shadow + 1% ramp dark-run after triage. timeline: triage within 12h, re-run config by EOD tomorrow.

dominic: if triage shows it's quant-induced, we can relax latency thresholds but keep hallucination as a gate. consider auto-retry with quant-profile fallback if latency improves but hallucination persists.

olin: +1. also add a short automated smoke that probes instruction-heavy prompts during preflight to catch this earlier.

rachel: thanks all. I'll update the canary ticket with next steps and add the alert rule. :thumbsup:

maya: ticket link: https://redwood/issue/MLCANARY-889 . logs: s3://redwood-internal/evals/1725012345-quant-bridge/. will post results of nf4-alt run here.
